properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-13, extending his own RNA analogy. Nothing here is intent and nothing has been chosen.

HIS WORDS: "going back to the RNA pairing discussion, can we have each project have a set of defined pair types that could facilitate the combining if two projects in a much faster manner?" — and, earlier in the same message, the shape he was reaching for: "not sure if one project carries a set of one side of the pairs and that would allow the other project to only line up with its corresponding pair on the other side."

⭐ THE ANALOGY IS PRECISE ABOUT WHY PAIRING IS FAST, and that is the real content of the idea. Four bases, two valid pairs, an alphabet fixed by chemistry. Matching is a LOOKUP, not a comparison. reflow2 today does comparison: `req:complementary-pairing` keys on `medium` PLUS `transport_security` PLUS `auth`, then falls back to fuzzy name resolution with a reported middle band a human must answer. Declared pair types would replace the fuzzy step with an exact one.

🛑 AND THE ANALOGY ALSO NAMES ITS OWN LIMIT, which is the honest counterweight. Bases pair by an alphabet that chemistry fixes GLOBALLY and nobody negotiates. Two organisations have no chemistry. A shared pair-type vocabulary requires prior agreement between the parties — and working WITHOUT prior agreement is exactly what the attribute key buys, in exactly the cross-organisation context reflow2 states as its operating breadth. The idea's power and its limit come from the same property.

═══ THE OPTIONS ═══

A — NOTHING. The attribute key already pairs two designs that never coordinated. Faster matching is not obviously the constraint. CHEAPEST, and the null hypothesis.

B — A DECLARED PAIR-TYPE VOCABULARY, his idea literally: each project publishes named types, and combining is a type-name join. FASTEST when both sides share the vocabulary; USELESS when they do not, and worse than useless if two orgs use one name for different contracts — a false pair is more dangerous than no pair, which is the failure the dynograph-foundation trial already produced once from the provider side.

C — ⭐ USE `SPECIFIES`, WHICH ALREADY EXISTS AND HAS NEVER BEEN DRAWN. The schema carries it: "A machine-readable contract artifact defines an entity — an OpenAPI / protobuf / JSON-schema / IDL file SPECIFIES an Interface (its authoritative contract)", with a `format` property. MEASURED 2026-08-13: **zero SPECIFIES edges in reflow2's design.** If two designs' Interfaces are both specified by the SAME artifact, matched on content hash, that is exact pairing with NO vocabulary to negotiate — THE HASH IS THE AGREEMENT. It is the ICD made first-class, which `Interface.designation` already gestures at when it cites 10 U.S.C. 4401 and "what an ICD publishes". Needs no new node type, no new edge type, no enum change, and no stamp move.

D — HYBRID, AND THE ONE THAT DEGRADES HONESTLY: exact when a shared contract artifact is present, attribute-key-plus-fuzzy-name when it is not. Two designs that have agreed get a precise seam; two that have not still get today's answer. Costs a second matching path and a rule for which wins.

═══ COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, recorded beside the idea ═══

⚠️ 1. THE STRONGEST — SPEED IS NOT THE CONSTRAINT, AND MAY NEVER BE. reflow2's own frontier reads seams 0% : ZERO of 73 component couplings run through a declared Interface. There is nothing to pair yet. Optimising the matching step while nothing is labelled is optimising past the actual blocker, which is that boundaries are unclassified.
   📌 STATUS 2026-08-13: PARTLY ADDRESSED. `cap:undeclared-seam-is-named` shipped (PR #167) and now NAMES those 73 pairs as one aggregate gap. It does not declare them — it asks. The blocker is now visible rather than silent.
⚠️ 2. THE FUZZY MIDDLE BAND IS NOT A DEFECT TO REMOVE. Asking a human about an uncertain name match is `dec:ask-not-repair` working as designed. Replacing it with exact lookup removes the question by removing the cases that raise it — which is only an improvement where the shared vocabulary is real.
⚠️ 3. A SHARED VOCABULARY IS A COORDINATION COST, and this project spends heavily to avoid exactly that: `dec:identity-out-of-band` refuses a registry that hands out ids, `dec:advisory-concurrency` refuses a lock manager. A pair-type registry is the same shape as the things twice rejected.
⚠️ 4. `SPECIFIES` IS UNUSED, SO THE SUBSTRATE IS UNTESTED. Zero edges means option C's mechanism has never run on real data, and every linking defect this project has found came from running the thing rather than reading it.

📌 WHERE THE IDEA IS STRONGEST, and it is narrower than "a vocabulary": WITHIN ONE OWNER'S NEIGHBOURHOOD. Ten reflow2 designs live under ~/project, all Anthony's. A shared pair-type vocabulary across designs one person controls is entirely achievable, needs no negotiation, and would make combining them mechanical. It is the cross-ORGANISATION case that cannot assume it — so the honest question may be whether reflow2 supports both, with the vocabulary as an optional accelerator over an attribute-based floor. That is option D.


═══════════ SHARPENED 2026-08-13, SAME SESSION ═══════════

Anthony then described the combining PROCESS step by step: "can first filter out interfaces in a graph. secondly, of the interfaces, can they be labeled as publisher, subscriber, or both. then you kind of have 3 RNA pairs. the agent then has the job of mapping publishers with subscribers (one RNA pair) and both with both. if the agent is unable to pair based on reason, you now have a gap or issue to solve."

⭐⭐ THE FIRST FINDING IS THAT HE RE-DERIVED THE BUILT ALGORITHM, and this is recorded as a NON-finding on purpose rather than filed as new. Verified against `crates/reflow2-core/src/seam.rs:464` rather than assumed: `offers = published | both`, `needs = required | both`. Three labels, four valid combinations — published↔required, published↔both, both↔required, both↔both — never like-with-like, which `two_publishers_never_pair_with_each_other` pins as a test. And the unpairable DO become findings, in five buckets: `paired` (the seam), `unmet_needs` (a subscriber nothing publishes), `dead_surface` (a publisher nobody subscribes to), `conflicts` (role-compatible but cannot connect on medium/transport_security/auth), `candidates` (the fuzzy middle band — the code comment reads "worth a human's attention, never acted on").

The RNA analogy was his on 2026-07-27 and produced `req:complementary-pairing`. Reasoning from it again nine days later reproduced the same algorithm from a different starting point. THAT IS CORROBORATION, NOT REPETITION — an analogy that regenerates the same structure twice is doing work rather than decorating a decision already made.

🛑 AND THE ONE GENUINE DELTA: "if the agent is unable to pair BASED ON REASON". His version has an AGENT JUDGEMENT step. The built version has none — pairing is a computed key end to end, and no LLM is consulted at any point. That opens three further options:

E — THE AGENT PROPOSES ON `candidates`, THE GRAPH STILL COUNTS, THE HUMAN STILL DECIDES. Let an agent argue for or against each middle-band pair in prose, ATTACHED to the candidate rather than resolving it. Exactly `dec:three-party-checks` — "the LLM speaks, the graph remembers and counts, the human decides" — applied to a band that currently arrives with a score and no argument. A score says HOW CLOSE two names are; it never says WHY they might be the same contract.

F — 📌 THE AGENT REASONS OVER `conflicts` INSTEAD, and this is the strongest narrow form. A conflict today says "you publish REST/JWT/TLS, I need REST/none/none, we cannot connect" — true, and silent on whether that is a real incompatibility or one side simply never filled in `auth`. An agent that has read both designs can tell "they left it unspecified" from "these genuinely disagree", and those need opposite actions. This is the one place a computed answer is PROVABLY incomplete, because `unspecified` is the honest default on three of the key's fields and the key cannot distinguish silence from disagreement.

G — THE AGENT PAIRS OUTRIGHT where the key is silent. RECORDED AS REJECTED-LEANING so it is not re-proposed by someone who has not read the trial: a false pair is worse than no pair, and the dynograph-foundation session already produced one from the computed side — "I require REST" matching an unauthenticated liveness probe. An LLM guessing would be the same failure with less traceability.

⚠️ 5. A FURTHER COUNTER-ARGUMENT ON E: the candidate band exists precisely so a HUMAN decides. Putting an agent between the score and the person risks the band being cleared by argument rather than by judgement, which is the erosion `dec:ask-not-repair` is written against.
⚠️ 6. AND `unlabelled` MUST STILL BE COUNTED whatever is chosen. `req:complementary-pairing` already requires it: a boundary nobody classified must not read as `internal`, or a design that never did the labelling pairs with nothing and reports a clean seam.


═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SHARPENED AGAIN 2026-08-13, AND THIS ONE MOVES THE QUESTION:
LINKABILITY IS THE USER'S ASSERTION; REFLOW2'S JOB IS REFINEMENT
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

ANTHONY'S WORDS, and they settle what pairing is FOR:

"maybe it is too much for two+ projects just to be linked kind of in an ad-hoc approach (something like a user saying 'link projectA and ProjectB' and just turning it over to reflow2 and the agent to figure out how. in defining flo2, I knew from the get go that it was going to have to use reflow2. it became a much more measured/deliberate approach of having flo2 read the reflow2 code and graph and then identifying (the agent) how it'd interface"

and then, decisively:

"I think the deliberate part of purposefully linking two projects is the user's responsibility that two projects can actually be linked. if projectA was a design for a house and ProjectB was design a python service for accounting, that is a failure on the user and ad-hoc/automatic linking can't occur (unless we do some very creative linking). I knew when I designed flo2 that it was going to use reflow2 - is the interface spec perfect? no, it is still in work, but I know the two projects can roughly interface with each other and precisely the point of all this is to use reflow2 to make a clearly defined and fully specified interface"

⭐⭐⭐ **THE CORRESPONDENCE IS AN INPUT, NOT AN OUTPUT.** That inverts the framing every option above assumed. reflow2 is not being asked whether a house design and an accounting service relate — asserting linkability is the USER'S job, and getting it wrong is a user error rather than a tool failure. What reflow2 is for is taking a roughly-known, still-in-work correspondence and driving it to a **clearly defined and fully specified interface**.

⇒ **WHICH MAKES `seam_report` THE LOAD-BEARING TOOL AND `pair_designs` THE CONVENIENCE**, and today the documentation has that backwards. `seam_report`'s own parameter doc reads: *"`pair_designs` computes these from complementary roles since 2026-07-30; supply them by hand only when a design has not declared its roles yet"* — treating the hand-supplied pair as a FALLBACK. Under Anthony's model the hand-supplied pair is the PRIMARY and correct input, and computed pairing is an accelerator for the case where nobody has asserted anything yet.

═══ MEASURED THE SAME DAY, AND IT SETTLES WHICH TOOL ANSWERS THE GOAL ═══

Full run recorded in `fact:reflow2-flo2-seam-measured-2026-08-13`. The two halves:

  COMPUTED (`pair_designs`, both designs as they stand)
    paired 0 · conflicts 10 · unmet_needs 5 · dead_surface 2 · candidates 1
    and with the role corrected in memory, the TRUE seam scores 64 while a WRONG
    match (ifc:graph-export, sharing the word "design") scores 81 and outranks it.

  ASSERTED (`seam_report`, pair supplied by hand: ifc:mcp-tools ↔ ifc:reflow2-design-api)
    agreed 3 · incompatible 0 · differs 0 · UNSTATED BY NOBODY 5
    → auth, transport_security, operations, error_model, payload_schema

⇒ **THE ASSERTED PAIR PRODUCES EXACTLY THE ANSWER HIS GOAL ASKS FOR** — the two projects are compatible as far as anything is stated, and five named axes stand between "roughly interfaces" and "fully specified". The computed path produced nothing usable on the same seam. That is the strongest evidence yet for the reframe, and it was obtained by RUNNING the two projects at each other rather than by reasoning about them.

🛑 AND IT CAUGHT REFLOW2 BEING THE UNDER-SPECIFIED SIDE. flo2 states `auth: none` and `transport_security: tls`; reflow2's own PUBLISHED `ifc:mcp-tools` states NEITHER — *"the side that assumed less finds out in production"*. Only a cross-project check surfaced it, which is an argument for linking as a DESIGN INSTRUMENT rather than only as a delivery step.

═══ WHAT THIS CHANGES ABOUT A/B/C/D, none of them yet taken ═══

· **A (nothing) is weakened.** Computed pairing found 0 on the one real seam and ranked a wrong match first; it is not currently sufficient for the deliberate case.
· **B (pair-type vocabulary) is answered rather than chosen.** Anthony's own framing supplies what B was reaching for without a registry: the user ASSERTS the pair. No shared alphabet is negotiated because the assertion is per-link, not per-vocabulary.
· **C (`SPECIFIES`) is now empirically motivated**, and is the durable form of the assertion: recording "this boundary of mine IS that boundary of yours" at the moment it is authored, with the content hash as the agreement, rather than re-deriving it from names later.
· **D (hybrid) survives unchanged** and is probably the shape: assertion first, computation as the accelerator.

📌 THE UNBUILT PIECE THIS EXPOSES: **there is no way to RECORD the correspondence.** flo2's `ifc:reflow2-design-api` exists BECAUSE someone read reflow2's `ifc:mcp-tools`; nothing in either graph says so, and the pair had to be re-supplied by hand at every run. `mirrors` on reflow2 returns 0, so the built mechanism for "I designed against your published surface, pinned at this version" has never been used on the pair of projects that most obviously calls for it. **The pairing information was free at design time and thrown away.**

NOT DECIDED.
properties.name: OPEN — how should two designs be paired: declared pair types, a shared contract artifact, or (SETTLED) the user asserting the correspondence and reflow2 refining it?
properties.rationale:
Recorded under the brainstorm skill so the thinking survives without being claimed as intent, and kept separate from the graph_id question because the two are unrelated. Worth keeping for one measured fact and one connection: SPECIFIES exists in the schema with a format property and has zero edges in reflow2's own design, so the mechanism for exact contract-based pairing is already built and never exercised; and the RNA analogy, which has already earned its place once by predicting that compatibility needs more than one point of contact, here argues BOTH ways — a fixed alphabet is why base pairing is fast AND why two organisations cannot borrow the trick.

⭐ THE AGENT-REASONING BRANCH IS SETTLED, 2026-08-13, ANTHONY'S WORD: "I agree with the approach without an agent 'reasoning'." Options E, F and G are CLOSED — no LLM enters the pairing loop, on candidates, on conflicts, or anywhere else. Pairing stays a computed key end to end.

WHAT THAT COSTS, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT DISCOVERED LATER AS A SURPRISE: option F was the strongest of the three and it named a real hole. A `conflict` says "you publish REST/JWT/TLS, I need REST/none/none" and CANNOT distinguish a genuine disagreement from one side never having filled in `auth` — because `unspecified` is the honest default on three of the key's fields. That gap does not close by itself. It now has to be closed some other way, if it is closed at all: by a detector that reports HOW MUCH of a conflict rests on unspecified fields, by the pairing report naming which side was silent, or by a human reading the two boundaries. Declining the agent does not make the computed answer complete; it means the completion must be computed or asked, never inferred.

WHY THIS IS CONSISTENT WITH THE PROJECT RATHER THAN A NARROWING OF IT: `dec:three-party-checks` gives the LLM the speaking role, not the counting one, and everything reflow2 computes is deliberately verdict-free — `granularity` refuses to call an observation a defect, `maturity` refuses to grade a band, `ility_report` refuses a score. An agent arguing a pair into or out of existence would be the LLM doing the counting.

⭐⭐ SHARPENED AGAIN 2026-08-13 AND THE QUESTION MOVED: Anthony settled that ASSERTING TWO PROJECTS CAN BE LINKED IS THE USER'S RESPONSIBILITY, not something reflow2 discovers — "if projectA was a design for a house and ProjectB was a design for a python service for accounting, that is a failure on the user." reflow2's job is refinement: taking a roughly-known correspondence and making it "clearly defined and fully specified." The correspondence is an INPUT.

That was then MEASURED against flo2 the same day (fact:reflow2-flo2-seam-measured-2026-08-13) and the measurement backs it: computed pairing returned 0 paired and ranked a wrong match above the right one, while the hand-asserted pair returned 0 incompatible, 3 agreed and 5 axes stated by nobody — exactly the punch-list his goal asks for. It also caught reflow2's own published boundary being the under-specified side. A/B/C/D remain open, but B is answered rather than chosen (a per-link assertion needs no negotiated vocabulary) and C is now the durable form of the assertion rather than a theoretical preference.
